standard_prerequisites: Divisors of meromorphic sections of an invertible sheaf, their orders along prime divisors, and the local finiteness of the divisors occurring in such a sum
The canonical section of the invertible sheaf attached to an effective Cartier divisor, its divisor class, and the computation of the divisor of a regular section as the intersection with the divisor
The key formula expressing the difference between the two ways of writing a cycle as a boundary, and the definition of the Gysin pullback along an effective Cartier divisor
core_obligations: Write the divisor of the meromorphic section as a locally finite sum over integral closed subspaces of the critical dimension, and arrange that the section is a generator on the complement of their union and that every component of the divisor is among them

Introduce the invertible sheaf of the effective Cartier divisor with its canonical section, and for each prime divisor choose generators of both sheaves at the henselization of the local ring at its generic point, insisting that the generator of the first sheaf is the canonical section whenever the prime divisor is not contained in the divisor
Express the coefficients of the meromorphic section and of the divisor class in terms of orders of the two quotients defining the sections in those henselizations

Identify the pullback of the divisor of the meromorphic section with a sum of divisors of restrictions of the local generators, using the computation of the divisor of a regular section as the intersection with the effective divisor

Identify the first Chern class capped with the divisor class with the corresponding sum using the same orders, and apply the key formula to obtain the rational equivalence between the two cycles; the boundary terms vanish at those prime divisors not contained in the effective divisor, which finishes the comparison
proof_roadmap: Put the meromorphic section and the effective divisor into a locally finite normal form with compatible local generators
Rewrite both the pullback of the divisor and the Chern class cap as sums weighted by orders along the prime divisors
Identify the individual summands through the divisor of a regular section
Apply the key formula and discard the vanishing boundary terms
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the identification of the Gysin pullback of the divisor of a meromorphic section with the first Chern class capped with the divisor class at source lines 3661-3670, label lemma-gysin-factors-general, whose proof occupies source lines 3672-3727. The proof is a local-to-global coefficient computation: the two cycles are first put into compatible normal forms along the prime divisors, with local generators chosen so that the generator of the divisor sheaf is the canonical section away from the effective divisor, then each cycle is written as a sum weighted by orders in henselized local rings, the individual summands are identified through the divisor of a regular section, and the equality is upgraded from an identity of cycles to a rational equivalence by the key formula, whose boundary terms vanish exactly at the prime divisors outside the effective divisor. The counted statement records neither the normal form nor the order computation.
